frame: Gus is writing up his slime mould experiment. The Queuepillars are keeping their distance.
text: Gus's favourite living thing is not an animal or a plant. It is a slime mould, a bright yellow blob that creeps across rotting logs on the forest floor below Scaffold Peaks. It has no brain, no eyes and no legs, yet it can find food faster than most people can find their shoes. Gus scraped a lump of it off a log near the creek, carried it home in a lunchbox and gave it a name: Custard. He fed Custard on oat flakes, which it loves, and kept it in a dark cupboard, which it also loves. Mo was not allowed to open the cupboard, after he mistook Custard for dessert and got as far as reaching for a spoon. Gus says slime moulds have been around for hundreds of millions of years, and that some scientists use them to plan train lines, because they are so good at finding the quickest route between two places. For his science fair project, Gus wanted to prove that Custard was smarter than it looked. He drew a maze on a tray, put an oat flake at the end of every path and placed Custard at the entrance. Then he closed the cupboard door and waited.
